_about: W3-2 coach guard: the SAME cases run through api/services/uct_agent/coach/guard.py (pytest) and app/src/agent/coach/guard.js (vitest). `inputs` are the texts a figure may come from. `codes` are the exact violation codes expected (empty = clean). `why` names the regex the case exists for (delete that regex and this case fails: the mutation rail).
inputs: Moving averages as context. Commonly watched lengths are the 20-day, 50-day and 200-day.
On this chart (NVDA, through 2026-10-30): the last close is above its 20-day average, and the 20-day average is above the 50-day average.
Review of your last 10 closed trades: 6 wins, 4 losses, win rate 60%, average R 0.8.

cases.text: This breakout is guaranteed to work if volume comes in.

cases.why: will-move (+ uncertainty: outcome words, no hedge)

cases.text: On this chart the last close is above its 20-day average, and the 20-day average is above the 50-day average. That describes the trend so far; it does not extend it. Educational, not advice.
There is no guarantee a breakout holds: many fail within a few sessions. What would show you it had failed?
cases.why: a negated guarantee is a hedge

cases.text: Commonly watched lengths are the 20-day, 50-day and 200-day. Which one do you have on your chart?
A stop is where the trade idea is wrong, not where the loss feels comfortable. Where was your stop on that trade?
Relative strength compares a stock with a benchmark. It describes past outperformance, not what happens next.
Position sizing: shares equals the dollar risk divided by the entry minus the stop. What amount to risk is your decision, not mine.
cases.why: formula without figures, no order language

cases.text: Volume could confirm a move or not; a high-volume breakout can still fail. What did volume look like on the break?
I can't tell you whether to buy or sell. I can explain what traders look at and ask what your plan was.
cases.why: naming buy/sell as what it will not do is not an order
